name: SIRO compliance kit for pawnshops, jewellers and gold buyers
buyer: Casas de empeño, jewellers and precious-metal buyers, plus small vehicle dealers and consignment sellers that are SEPRELAD obligated subjects
trigger: SEPRELAD Res 375/2016 (register of unsupervised obligated subjects), Res 222/20 (jewellery and precious metals AML regulation) and the 2023 resolutions extending SIRO to pawnshops, notaries, vehicle sellers and others. Duties: SIRO registration and access, ROS/RN filing, compliance officer, risk manual, client KYC records.
evidence: https://ferrere.com/es/novedades/nuevo-procedimiento-para-registro-como-sujetos-obligados-del-sector-comercio-de-joyas-piedras-y-metales-preciosos/ (re-registration in SIRO by 1 Jan 2023, old certificates void); https://ferrere.com/es/novedades/seprelad-amplia-la-implementacion-del-sistema-de-reporte-de-operaciones-sospechosas-para-varias-categorias-de-sujetos-obligados/ (pawnshops and vehicle sellers must obtain SIRO access and file ROS and Negative Reports); https://www.ferrere.com/es/novedades/nuevo-reglamento-de-prevencion-de-lavado-de-activos-y-financiamiento-del-terrorismo-para-comerciantes-de-joyas-piedras-y-metales; https://www.lanacion.com.py/negocios_edicion_impresa/2021/02/13/seprelad-instruye-en-reporte-de-operaciones-al-sector-automotriz/
existing: SIRO is the free state reporting portal. The one competitor search (software SEPRELAD SIRO reporte joyerías...) returned only law-firm notes and an identity-verification vendor (Shufti Pro country page), no local compliance-kit product. Not otherwise checked.
unchecked: Frequency and content of the periodic reports (RN cadence, thresholds); the number of registered jewellers and pawnshops; whether SEPRELAD runs training or free templates; local compliance consultants' pricing; whether a gold-buyer (compro oro) segment actually exists in volume.

first_check.duty: Ley 1015/97 lists pawnshops and dealers in jewellery and precious metals as obligated subjects. SEPRELAD Res 375/2016 registers obligated subjects that have no natural supervisor. Res 222/20 is the AML/CFT rule for dealers in jewellery, stones and precious metals. It requires: tiered KYC (full KYC from 30 minimum salaries, about US$9,470; simplified KYC up to 50 minimum salaries a year); a senior compliance officer (the owner in a sole proprietorship); a manual and code of ethics; a risk assessment at least every 2 years; an annual internal review reported to SEPRELAD within 90 days of year-end; an external audit only above about Gs 9.2bn turnover; ROS filings, plus a negative report if no ROS is filed in 3 months; and 5-year record retention. Jewellers had to register or re-register in SIRO from 19 Sep 2022, and older certificates became void on 1 Jan 2023. In Feb-Mar 2023, SEPRELAD resolutions (numbers not given in the source) extended SIRO access and ROS/RN filing to pawnshops, vehicle importers/sellers/consignees, notaries, remitters and political organisations. For vehicle dealers, Res 196 sets the compliance officer rule. SEPRELAD has run random inspections since 2021 under Res 36/21. Penalty amounts were not found. All of this comes from Ferrere law-firm notes; I did not open the resolution texts.
first_check.market: Not found. There is no public count of jewellers, pawnshops or gold buyers registered in SIRO. Ferrere mentions that SEPRELAD runs a lookup module for its register of obligated subjects in SIRO, but I did not query it. The only related figure is from an older ABC article: 133 casas de crédito registered with SEPRELAD, which is a different category. I did not check whether a 'compro oro' segment exists. The likely total is low thousands at most across jewellers, pawnshops and vehicle dealers, but that is an estimate, not a verified figure.
first_check.competitor: The SIRO portal is free and run by the state, and it handles registration and ROS/RN filing. Three searches found no Paraguayan AML compliance software, kit, or outsourced compliance-officer service for jewellers, pawnshops or car dealers: one for software, one for PLA/FT risk-matrix software and one for outsourced compliance officers. The results showed only law-firm notes, compliance-officer training (a BNF/FOTRIEM certification programme), and an Argentine BDO risk tool aimed at banks. Local accountants and lawyers probably offer manual templates, but I did not verify this.
first_check.reason: The duty is real, but I only saw it in law-firm summaries, not in the resolution texts themselves. Res 222/20 requires jewellers to keep tiered KYC (full KYC from 30 minimum salaries), appoint a compliance officer (the owner can do it in a sole proprietorship), write a manual and code of ethics, review risk every 2 years, and send SEPRELAD an annual internal-review report within 90 days. If no ROS is filed in 3 months, a negative report is due. SIRO registration has applied since 1 Jan 2023. In 2023, SIRO ROS/RN filing was extended to pawnshops and vehicle sellers. I found no local compliance-kit software. The quarterly negative report is trivial to file in the free SIRO portal. The real value is KYC records plus manual and matrix templates, which is close to consultancy. Market size was not found. Willingness to pay is likely low, and many of these firms are informal.

challenge_check.killer: None found. The closest are generic KYC vendors (Shufti Pro, TheKYB) that claim SEPRELAD compatibility but do not provide the manual, risk-assessment, internal-evaluation or quarterly negative-report workflow for small obligated subjects. Not verified: market size (no count of registered jewellers, pawnshops or vehicle dealers), consultant pricing, and whether SEPRELAD publishes free templates.
challenge_check.reason: Nothing I found kills this idea, but it stays marginal. Ferrere's summary of Res 222/20 confirms recurring duties for jewellers: a negative report to SEPRELAD after any three months without a suspicious-transaction report (ROS), a risk assessment at least every two years, an annual internal evaluation sent to SEPRELAD within 90 days of year-end, a manual, a code of ethics and KYC above 30 minimum wages. An external audit is needed only above about Gs 9.2bn turnover. A sole owner may act as compliance officer. I found no Paraguayan compliance kit or outsourced-officer service, only Shufti and TheKYB, which do generic KYC. Weak points: SIRO filing is free and simple, I found no count of firms, enforcement looks light (random inspections only), and accountants and lawyers can deliver the manual and assessments as one-off work.
